Subject: Re: Recap: Data handling & support access for River Mortgage (next steps)

Hi Lauren —

Appreciate the clear recap. I filled the attached matrix and added notes inline; main points below:

- PII in scope: first/last name, DOB, SSN (last 4 required for verification), bank account numbers (ACH), loan application docs that may contain PHI in rare cases. No PCI payment card data in scope.
- Residency: production and backups must remain in AWS us-east-1. DR may be in us-east-2 but encrypted and under same residency controls.
- Retention: customer records = 7 years (regulatory); logs/audit trails = 1 year (readily queryable), archived logs = 7 years offline.
- Logs required: access logs (user & service), admin action audit trails, API request/response metadata (not full model outputs unless requested under support incident), and key rotation events.
- Support access / break-glass: We require a documented two-step approval (on-call manager + security lead) before escalation. Temporary elevated access limited to 4 hours, with automated session recording and mandatory post-incident report.
- KMS: We prefer customer-managed keys (CMK) with KMS in our account, but will consider provider-managed keys for the pilot if we're satisfied with key access controls and audit logs.

I attached: PII_handling_matrix.xlsx (completed) and a short security_overview.pdf that summarizes our compliance constraints.

Next steps: please have Marcus draft a short note on Redwood's standard break-glass workflow and whether time-limited support tokens and session recording can be enforced. We can then lock a 30-min slot for Wed 24 Feb.

Thanks,
Sofia Patel
Head of Security & Compliance | River Mortgage
sofia.patel@rivermortgage.com | +1 (212) 555-0189

Attachments: PII_handling_matrix.xlsx, security_overview.pdf

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sofia Patel <sofia.patel@rivermortgage.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 09:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Data handling & support access for River Mortgage (next steps)

Thanks, Sofia — that matrix is very helpful. Quick technical notes / proposals from our side (so we can be explicit on the Wed deep dive):

1) Residency & backups: Redwood can pin data to us-east-1 for active workloads. For backups, we support same-region encrypted snapshots; cross-region DR (us-east-2) is possible only if the customer approves the encryption boundary and key policies.

2) Retention model: We support per-customer retention policies. For your regulatory 7-year requirement we can keep object-level snapshots offline and provide restoration/fulfillment processes. For logs, real-time retention is configurable; default short-term retention is 90 days, hot logs. We can tier to cold archive for 7 years (S3 Glacier-like) with retrieval SLAs.

3) Logging / audit: We capture admin actions, token-based service access, API call metadata, and option to record model input/outputs only when explicitly triggered by a support incident (flagged, encrypted, and tagged). Audit exports available to your SIEM via secure log-forwarding.

4) Support access / break-glass: We recommend a time-limited support tunnel using short-lived JWTs + ephemeral session keys. Proposed flow:
   - Break-glass request submitted via portal (reason, affected resource, ticket)
   - Two approvers required (on-call manager + security lead)
   - Token issued for max 4 hours with scoped RBAC and mandatory session recording (WORM log of keystrokes + video optional)
   - Automatic email notification to your security mailbox and an immutable audit record in our audit log.

5) KMS: We support both provider-managed KMS and customer-managed (bring-your-own) keys. CMK is the higher-assurance option; if you choose CMK we provide clear policies for grant/revoke and key-rotation workflows.

Attached is a short stub: support_tunnel_design.txt outlining endpoints and token lifecycle. For Wed, I can present the RBAC role mapping (least-privilege templates) and a short demo of the break-glass portal.

Questions for Sofia / Tom before the call:
- Do you require model input/outputs to be retained by default or only when support explicitly requests them?
- Confirm the minimum log retention the team needs in a hot state (queryable) vs. archived state.

I'll block time Wed 24 Feb 10:00-10:30 PT unless you prefer a different window.

—Marcus
